lines.say: Your database queries are fast. Your orders page is slow. The bug lives between them.
lines.show: Your database queries are fast. Your orders page is slow. The bug lives between them.

lines.say: First, your code asks for the last hundred orders. One trip to the database.
lines.show: First, your code asks for the last hundred orders. One trip to the database.

lines.say: Then for each order, it goes back to fetch the customer. One trip per order. A hundred more.
lines.show: Then for each order, it goes back to fetch the customer. One trip per order. A hundred more.

lines.say: Every trip waits on the network and the database. Those small waits add up. That is the slow part.
lines.show: Every trip waits on the network and the database. Those small waits add up. That is the slow part.

lines.say: This is the N plus one problem. One query for the list, then one query for each of the hundred orders. A hundred and one queries.
lines.show: This is the N plus one problem. One query for the list, then one query for each of the hundred orders. A hundred and one queries.

lines.say: The fix: get the orders, then ask for all their customers together in one query. Two trips total.
lines.show: The fix: get the orders, then ask for all their customers together in one query. Two trips total.

lines.say: Your ORM can often batch this for you with eager loading. Check which queries it actually generates.
lines.show: Your ORM can often batch this for you with eager loading. Check which queries it actually generates.

lines.say: Log the queries for one page load. If the count grows with every row on screen, that is your clue. A few queries can replace hundreds.
